tags.name: Agents
tags.description:
How an AI agent that a user brings, such as one running on their own computer, imports the question sets it made into their QBank, reads how the user answered them, and adds, changes and deletes their content as they can in QBank, over plain HTTP, with a key of its own instead of the user's session.

**Pairing.** Nobody copies a key: the agent asks for one, the user approves it in QBank, and the agent picks it up (OAuth 2.0 device authorization, RFC 8628, in this API's words).

1. The agent starts a pairing with `POST /api/agent-pairings`, sending no key: its `name`, which the user will see (such as "My MacBook agent"), and the `scopes` it wants. It gets back `deviceCode`, its own secret for this pairing, and `userCode`, such as `BCDF-GHJK`, to show the user. Both last 10 minutes (`expiresAt`).
2. Signed in to QBank, the user enters the code. The app shows the agent's name and scopes, each in plain words (`scopeTexts`, from `POST /api/agent-pairings/lookup`), and the user approves (`POST /api/agent-pairings/approve`) or denies (`POST /api/agent-pairings/deny`) it. Approving gives the key to the account signed in. The name is only what the agent says it is, so the user approves only a code their own agent is showing them.
3. Meanwhile the agent polls `POST /api/agent-pairings/token` with its `deviceCode`, waiting `interval` seconds (5 at first) after each answer. Until the user answers it gets 400 `authorization_pending`; a poll that comes too soon gets 400 `slow_down` and a longer `interval` to keep from then on. Once approved, it gets 200 with `token`, the key (`qbk_...`), exactly once: QBank keeps only its hash, and the pairing is used up. 400 `access_denied` means the user denied it; 400 `expired_token` means the pairing ran out or its key was handed over already. Either way the agent starts again.
4. The agent keeps the key in the operating system's keychain (the macOS Keychain on a Mac), never in a file, a repository, or a log, and sends it on every call below as `Authorization: Bearer qbk_...`.

Starting is limited: one address may start a few pairings in 10 minutes, and only so many may wait at once, whoever started them; past either, 429 `too_many_pairings` with `retryAfterSeconds`.

**The user's keys.** `GET /api/agent-keys` lists the account's keys: each one's name, scopes, when it was made, and when it was last used. `POST /api/agent-keys/{id}/revoke` stops one at once and for good. A key is never shown again after the agent picks it up, and each account sees and revokes only its own.

**Scopes.** An operation tagged Agents lets a key in when the key has any one of the scopes its security names. `import` reaches checking and importing question files, and reading the account's semesters, courses and sets to do it. `read` reaches the user's answers, read-only (see Reading below). `manage` reaches everything `import` does and every change the user can make to their own content (see Changing below). A key may have any of them; a key keeps the scopes it was approved with, so an agent that needs another pairs again and the user approves the new key.

**Importing with the key.**

1. Find the course: `GET /api/semesters` lists the account's semesters with their courses (match `code`) and its study topics (match `title`).
2. Check every file before importing any: `POST /api/imports/check` with `{"source": "<the file>"}`. `ok: false` lists the `errors` that block it; `warnings` do not. `kind` is `exam` for an exam set, such as exam twins: a file meant as exam twins that comes back `practice` is not one, so import nothing.
3. Import each file: `POST /api/imports` with `source` and `courseId` (or `newCourse` or `newTopic`), and `folderName` or `folderId` (without either, the course's Unsorted folder); practice sets first, then their exam twins. Leave `decision` out, or send `import`.
   - 201: the set landed: `courseId`, `folderId`, `folderName`, `setId`, `setKind`, its `warnings`, and `importedByAgent` naming this key.
   - 409: a current set of the same kind and name is already in the course, and nothing was written. Read it with `GET /api/practice-sets/{setId}` to tell whether it holds the same questions, and tell the user: they decide in QBank whether to replace it. A key without `manage` never replaces a set or adds a second of the same name (`decision` `replace` or `separate` answers 403); with `manage`, see Changing below.
   - 400 `invalid_import`, with `errors` and `warnings`: the file fails the check. Another 400 names what is wrong with the course or folder choice in `message`.
   - 404: that course or folder is not the account's.
4. Confirm where the sets landed: `GET /api/courses/{courseId}`. Each folder in `folders` lists its `sets` and `examSets` by title, each with `importedByAgent`, so the agent can tell the user "Week 5 now has Set 1 and Set 2, and their exam twins".

**Reading the user's answers with the key.** So the agent can aim its next questions at what the user finds hard. A `read` key only reads: it never answers a question, starts or ends an exam, clears Review, or changes anything else, and its reads write nothing in QBank but the key's `lastUsedAt`. It reads its own account's answers only: another account's course or exam answers 404, as an id that names nothing does, and a key the admin approved reads none (403 `agent_key_not_allowed`).

1. Where the user stands, topic by topic: `GET /api/me/standing`. Every course and study topic of the account, each with `byTopic`: for each topic its question files name, how many current questions it has (practice and exam bank), how many the user has answered, and what their latest answers were: fully right, partly right, missed, guessed, points of `maxPoints`, and how many are in Review. A topic with many answers and few fully right is a weak spot; one with few answers is not practiced yet. Its course ids are the ones the reads below take.
2. What the user missed or guessed in a course: `GET /api/courses/{id}/review`, with `?filter=missed`, `partial` or `guessed` for one kind. The course's Review list as the Review screen shows it, newest first: each practice question whose latest answer was not fully right or was a guess, with its topic, folder, set and mark. A question leaves the list when the user answers it fully right without guessing, or clears the list.
3. One exam's result: `GET /api/exams/{id}`, with an exam's id from the export (`studySessions` whose `mode` is `exam`). Its questions in the order served, and once it has ended, `result`: points, fully right, partly right, missed, guessed and not answered, by folder and by clinical judgment step, and each question's mark. `finishedAt` null with `endsAt` past means the user's time ran out and the end is recorded when their app next opens the exam; until then it has no `result`.
4. Everything: `GET /api/me/export`, the user's whole history as one JSON file: every answer they gave, each question's latest answer, every Review list, course scores, and every study session, exams included. It grows with every answer; for where the user stands, the standing is enough.

**Changing the user's content with the key.** A `manage` key adds, changes and deletes the account's own content through the same operations, with the same checks and answers, as the user's own app: everything in it is the user's, so do what the user asked and tell them what changed. It reaches the account's own content only: another account's id answers 404, as an id that names nothing does, and a key the admin approved changes nothing (403 `agent_key_not_allowed`).

- Semesters, courses and study topics: `POST /api/semesters`, `PATCH /api/semesters/{id}` (rename, archive), `POST /api/courses`, `POST /api/topics`, `PATCH /api/courses/{id}` (rename, move to another semester, archive), `PUT /api/topic-order`.
- Folders: `POST /api/courses/{id}/folders`, `PATCH /api/folders/{id}` (rename, put on a page or take off one), `PUT /api/courses/{id}/folder-order`, and `POST /api/practice-sets/{id}/move` to move a set to another folder.
- Pages: `POST /api/courses/{id}/course-exams` and `PUT /api/course-exams/{id}` (rename, set its folders, its primer link and its `badge`: `exam`, `concept`, `study`, or null for none). Deleting a page (below) deletes the page alone: its folders, their sets and the user's answers stay, in the course's Folders list until Undo.
- Sets and their questions: a set's questions change through its file. `POST /api/imports` adds a set (see Importing above); with `decision` `replace` its file becomes the set's new version, and the version before stays for Restore; with `separate` it is added beside the set of the same name. `POST /api/practice-sets/{id}/restore` brings back the version before.
- Deleting, always in three steps, as the user deletes: read the preview (`GET /api/practice-sets/{id}/delete-preview`, `GET /api/folders/{id}/delete-preview`, `GET /api/course-exams/{id}/delete-preview`, `GET /api/courses/{id}/delete-preview`), tell the user its `message` and do it only when they want it gone, then send its `confirm` with the delete (`DELETE /api/practice-sets/{id}?confirm=...`, `/api/folders/{id}`, `/api/course-exams/{id}`, `/api/courses/{id}`). Without `confirm` the delete answers 409 `confirmation_required` (only an empty folder or a page with no folders needs none), and when anything changed since the preview, 409 `deletion_changed`; either way nothing is deleted. Nothing is ever removed: what a key deletes goes to Recently deleted (`GET /api/courses/{id}/deleted`, `GET /api/deleted-courses`) exactly as the user's own deletes do, with `deletedByAgent` naming the key, and Undo (`POST /api/practice-sets/{id}/undo-delete`, `/api/folders/{id}/undo-delete`, `/api/course-exams/{id}/undo-delete`, `/api/courses/{id}/undo-delete`) brings it back as it was, for the user in QBank or for the key, for 30 days.

**What every one of these can answer for the key:** 401 `invalid_agent_key` (QBank does not know it) or `agent_key_revoked` (the user revoked it): pair again. 403 `agent_key_not_allowed`: its scopes do not cover this. 403 `must_change_password`: the account has a temporary password, and nothing works until the user signs in and picks their own. 503 `auth_unavailable`.

**What a key never does.** Every other operation, pairing and the user's keys included, answers a request that carries a key with 403 `agent_key_not_allowed` before reading it: a key never answers a question, starts or ends an exam, clears Review, or deletes a past exam, since the user's answers are theirs alone; never removes anything for good; never makes questions with Make questions; never changes a password, a passkey or an account; never reaches Admin or another account; and never pairs, approves, lists or revokes keys. Those need the user's signed-in session.

tags.name: Agent keys
tags.description: The user's side of pairing, and the account's agent keys: a signed-in session only (the session cookie, or the token from sign-in), never an agent key. Each account sees, answers for, and revokes only its own. See Agents for the whole flow.

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: The session cookie a browser holds after sign-in (`__Secure-better-auth.session_token` over HTTPS).

sessionToken.description: The token from sign-in (SignedIn.token), as the iPhone app sends it.

agentKey.description: An agent key from pairing (see the Agents tag), as `Authorization: Bearer qbk_...`. It reaches only the operations whose security names it, with the scopes listed there; every other operation answers it with 403 agent_key_not_allowed.

archivedAt.description: When she archived it, by hand, or null. Archived semesters are still listed; the screens group them last.

kind.description: `topic` for a study topic: a course with no semester, which the screens call by its title (its code is empty). Everything inside it, its pages included, works as in a course. `course` for every course.

folderCount.description: Her folders in the course, empty ones included: the course card's "N folders".

kind.description: `topic` for a study topic: a course with no semester, which the screens call by its title (its code is empty). Everything inside it, its pages included, works as in a course. `course` for every course.

semester.description: Its semester. Null exactly for a topic.

questionCount.description: Practice questions. Exam-bank questions are counted per week.

examQuestionCount.description: How many questions an exam over every week draws from: each week's exam bank, or its practice questions when it has none.

examTimeLimitSeconds.description: The time an exam over every week gets: 60 minutes for 40 questions, or 1.5 minutes a question when there are fewer (see ExamSetup.rules).

weekCount.description: Legacy: how many folder names hold practice sets, so two folders with the same name count once. Use folderCount.

folderCount.description: Her folders in the course, empty ones included: the course card's "N folders".

examBankCount.description: Exam-bank questions in its folders, asked only on exams. 0 when they have no exam bank.

weeks.description: Legacy, for clients from before folders: her folders that hold sets, by name (label), in week order. Two folders with the same name show as one week. Use folders.

folders.description: Every folder of the course, empty ones included: each page's folders, pages in the order of exams, then the folders on no page (the course's Folders list); each list in her order.

exams.description: The course's pages, such as Exam 1, each with its folders, in the order they were added. Empty until one is made.

importedByAgent.description: The agent key that imported this version of the set, such as the user's own AI agent (see the Agents tag): show it as "Imported by your agent". Null when it was imported in the app or QBank made it. It stays after the key is revoked.

id.description: Its agent key, as GET /api/agent-keys lists it.

name.description: The name the agent paired with, such as My MacBook agent.
Unique within its list, ignoring case: within its page, or within the course's Folders list (no page). Two pages may each have a First Pass.

examPageId.description: The page (CourseDetail.exams) it is on, or null when it is only in the course's Folders list. A folder is on one page at most. A folder of a page she deleted is null, in the Folders list after the folders there, until Undo puts it back on the page.

sortOrder.description: Its place in its list (its page's folders, or the Folders list), smallest first. Her own order: PUT /api/courses/{id}/folder-order.

sets.description: Its practice sets, by title. Every version of a set is in the same folder, so Restore never moves it.

examBankCount.description: Questions in its exam sets, asked only on exams: the "Exam bank: 14 questions, exams only" line under its sets. 0 when it has none.

examSets.description: Its exam sets (its exam bank), by title, each asked only on exams. Empty when it has none. One can be deleted on its own: GET /api/practice-sets/{id}/delete-preview.

importedByAgent.description: The agent key that imported this version of the set, such as the user's own AI agent (see the Agents tag): show it as "Imported by your agent". Null when it was imported in the app or QBank made it. It stays after the key is revoked.

weekLabels.description: Legacy: the names of its folders, in the page's order. Use folderIds.

folderIds.description: Its folders (CourseDetail.folders with this examPageId), in her order on the page.

linkUrl.description: The page's primer: a web address she opens from the page, or null. QBank shows it as a link and renders nothing.

badge.description: What the page is for, or null for no badge. Set and taken off with PUT /api/course-exams/{id}; a new page has none unless POST sent one.

PageBadge.description: What a page is for, shown as a small tag beside its name: `exam` (Exam), `concept` (Concept) or `study` (Study).

folderIds.description: The folders on this page, in the order she wants them. A folder of another page is refused with 409, naming it ("First Pass is in Exam 2."); move it with PATCH /api/folders/{id} first. A folder taken off the page goes to the end of the course's Folders list. Send folderIds or weekLabels, not both; with neither, POST makes an empty page and PUT keeps its folders.

weekLabels.description: Legacy, for clients from before folders: folder names, each meaning the folder of that name already on this page, else the one on no page. The page holds them in week order.

linkUrl.description: Its primer link, an http or https address of at most 2,000 characters. A value with no scheme:// is stored with one added: http:// for a tailnet or local host (a name ending in .ts.net, a single-label host, an IP address, localhost, or any address with a port) and https:// otherwise. Null or empty takes it off; left out, PUT keeps the page's link.

badge.description: Its badge. Null takes it off; left out, PUT keeps the page's badge and POST makes a page with none.

examPageId.description: The page to make it on. Without it, or null, it goes in the course's Folders list.

name.description: Its new name. Only the name changes: its sets, their progress, its page and her past exams stay with it.

examPageId.description: Put it on this page, at the end of its folders, or take it off its page with null, to the end of the Folders list. Leave it out to keep its page.
